text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
EqualTo(x, y) ::: x is equal to y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
RentAmount(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is $y.
MoveInWith(x, y) ::: Person x moves in with pet y.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: The security deposit at building x is $y.
WillRent(x) ::: Person x will rent an apartment.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (DepositRequired(x) → ∃y (SecurityDeposit(x, y) ∧ (EqualTo(y, RentAmount(x, month)) ∨ y > RentAmount(x, month)))) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building. The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Cat(tom) ∧ MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat. Cats are pets.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ∧ RentAmount(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building. The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
WillRent(tom) ↔ (MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ∧ SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, deposit) ∧ deposit ≤ 1500) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, 2000) ∨ SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, deposit) ∧ deposit > 2000 ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
